quickAnswer: Stow has no vacant housing at all in the 2022 ACS (0 of 2,613 units, the lowest vacancy rate of the 50 towns we serve), and 53.7% of homes heat with oil. Hudson Light & Power Department, a municipal utility, supplies electricity.
body: ## Every home occupied

The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS) counts 2,613 housing units in Stow, and all 2,613 are occupied. A vacancy rate of 0.0% is the lowest of the 50 towns Mass HVAC serves, against 3.6% for the middle town. Owners occupy 2,208 households (84.5%) and renters 405 (15.5%). The median owner-occupied home is worth $633,900, above the $579,150 of the middle town.
With no empty houses on the count, every failed heating or cooling system lands on a household that lives there.
## Farm and orchard land until the 1950s

Stow was incorporated in 1683 with about 40 square miles and then gave up land to Harvard, Shirley, Boxborough, Hudson and Maynard until it reached its present 18.1 square miles. According to Wikipedia, the town was primarily sparsely settled farm and orchard land until the 1950s, apart from factories at Assabet Village and Rock Bottom, which later became Maynard and Gleasondale.

The ACS age bands show where the housing sits today. 707 homes (27.1%) date from 1960 to 1979, the largest single band, and 533 (20.4%) from 1980 to 1999. Another 472 (18.1%) go back to 1939 or earlier and 324 (12.4%) to 1940 to 1959. The newest homes are a real share: 577 (22.1%) are from 2000 or later, and 308 (11.8%) from 2010 on, the 11th-highest share of the 50 towns. The median home was built in 1975, exactly the median for all 50. Overall, 1,503 homes (57.5%) predate 1980.
## Oil, propane and a gas main for one home in four

Fuel oil or kerosene heats 1,404 occupied homes (53.7%, 15th-highest). Utility gas serves 661 (25.3%), electricity 311 (11.9%) and bottled or tank gas 219 (8.4%, 12th-highest). Wood is a footnote at 6 homes. Oil is the leading fuel by a wide margin, and propane is more common than in the typical town, where it sits at 4.5%.

For a replacement decision, that gives four groups: oil, gas on a main, electric, and propane. An oil home may weigh a new oil system against a heat pump. An electric-heat home is a natural heat pump candidate. A gas home can stay with gas, or look at electrifying if the owner prefers.
## The Army, the river and the apartments

A few details from the town's history bear on the ground under the buildings. In 1942 the U.S. Army seized about one-tenth of the town's land for a munitions storage facility, which became part of the Assabet River National Wildlife Refuge in 2005. The Assabet River flows through Stow from west to east, and the flood of March 2010 reached 2,500 cubic feet per second, against an average that falls under 100 in summer. Lake Boon, White's Pond and Elizabeth Brook add to the town's water.

The town also has apartments and small buildings. 272 homes are in buildings of five or more units (10.4%), 141 in buildings of three or four (5.4%) and 19 in two-unit buildings (0.7%), for 432 units (16.5%) in multi-unit buildings. Detached houses are 79.8% of the stock, which ranks 23rd, and attached townhouse units number 96.
## The municipal electric rule

Hudson Light & Power Department is the town's electric utility, and it is municipal, so the usual Mass Save pathway is narrower than in a town served by National Grid. For the 661 gas homes, check Mass Save. For the oil and propane homes, ask Hudson Light & Power first. The [heat pump page](/cities/stow/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) has the terms.

faq.q: Is it true there are no vacant homes in Stow?
faq.a: That is what the 2022 ACS estimate shows: 0 vacant out of 2,613 housing units, a 0.0% vacancy rate and the lowest of the 50 towns we serve. It is an estimate with a margin of error, but it means every housing unit counted is lived in, so a heating failure lands on someone's household.

faq.q: Can I get a Mass Save heat pump rebate in Stow?
faq.a: Sometimes. The electric utility is municipal, so the answer depends on how your home heats. Gas homes and oil or propane homes can end up on different paths, and Hudson Light & Power Department is the first call for the latter. Confirm Mass Save terms at masssave.com.

faq.q: Should I replace my Stow oil boiler with a heat pump?
faq.a: It depends on the house and the rebate path. With 53.7% of Stow homes on oil, a heat pump is a common comparison. The home's heating load is assessed first, then a new oil system, a heat pump or a combination can be compared on that basis.

faq.q: Are Stow's newest homes different to heat and cool?
faq.a: They can be. The ACS counts 577 homes built in 2000 or later and 308 since 2010, the 11th-highest share of the 50 towns. Newer houses tend to be tighter, with ducts or ventilation planned in, while the 1,503 homes built before 1980 vary a lot more in insulation and air leakage.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Oil heats 1,404 Stow homes, tank gas 219 and utility gas 661, so a replacement often starts with choosing between those fuels and a heat pump. Stow's tank-gas share ranks 12th of 50.
body: ## Four fuel groups under one town name

Fuel oil serves 53.7% of Stow's occupied homes, 15th among the 50 towns, and utility gas 25.3%, 36th. Electricity serves 311 homes, tank gas 219 and wood just 6, with 12 more on other fuels or coal. The tank-gas share, 8.4%, is nearly double the 4.5% of the middle town, so propane work is a real part of the town's heating.
### Oil

The 1,404 oil homes can stay with oil, convert to gas where a main exists, or move to a heat pump. Staying with oil keeps the tank and chimney. Switching to gas means a main at the road, a new line into the house and a venting plan.
### Tank gas

Propane equipment needs correct regulator placement, gas piping and venting. Gas fuel work, whether on a main or a tank, requires a licensed plumber or gas fitter to pull the permit in Massachusetts, and a final inspection normally follows. The building department can describe its process.
### Gas on a main
The 661 homes on a main usually replace like for like. Their owners can also consider a heat pump for cooling and mild-weather heating, with the gas unit kept for cold days.
### Fit with the house

The median Stow home dates to 1975, and the biggest age band is 1960 to 1979 with 707 homes. Piping, baseboard and ducts from the original build may outlast the boiler. The heating load is worked out first, so the new unit is not just a copy of the old one.
### Renters

Stow has 405 renter households. In a rented unit the heating-season floor is 68 F during the day, 7 a.m. to 11 p.m., and 64 F overnight. Landlords pay for heat unless the lease states otherwise. Treat this as general information, not legal advice.
### Every unit is occupied

The ACS counts no vacant units in Stow, so a no-heat failure reaches a household at once. We take emergency calls 24/7 at (508) 786-8755, and written estimates are free before work starts. More on the town is on the [city page](/cities/stow).

faq.q: Can I convert from oil to propane in Stow?
faq.a: Often it can be done, though it is a full conversion with new equipment, gas piping, a tank location and a permit. With 219 homes already on tank gas, the setup is not unusual here. Compare the total cost with a plain oil replacement and with a heat pump.

faq.q: Is a wood stove a real heat source in Stow?
faq.a: Only 6 Stow homes, 0.2%, list wood as the main fuel, so a stove is mostly a supplement. A stove owner should have the chimney and flue inspected before winter, and should not count on the stove alone during a long outage.

faq.q: When should a Stow boiler be replaced instead of repaired?
faq.a: Wear on a single component of a newer boiler is normally worth fixing. A cracked heat exchanger, or a run of breakdowns on aging equipment, points the other way. Request both options in writing, and weigh them side by side.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Detached houses are 79.8% of Stow's housing, and 432 units sit in multi-unit buildings. Central air suits houses with usable ducts, while ductless can serve additions and rooms the ducts never reached.
body: ## Cooling a town of houses and mid-size buildings

The ACS counts 2,085 detached houses in Stow, 23rd of 50 for share. It also counts 96 attached townhouse units, 19 homes in two-unit buildings, 141 in buildings of three or four units and 272 in buildings of five or more. The mix of detached houses and larger buildings sets the cooling plan.
### Detached houses

A detached house usually leaves room for an outdoor condenser. Whether central cooling is practical depends on ducts, and homes that predate common central air can lack them. Where new ducts would mean cutting into finished walls, ductless is frequently the easier path.
### Larger buildings
The 272 units in buildings of five or more may have limited outdoor space for equipment. Mini-splits can help, but the owner or association has to approve where outdoor units go.
### Newer houses

Stow's 577 homes built in 2000 or later, 22.1% of the stock, include 308 from 2010 on, the 11th-highest share. Newer houses may already have ducts able to carry cooling, while their tighter shells make ventilation worth a look.
### Electric heat
Electricity heats 311 Stow homes, 11.9%, the 20th-highest share. Where electric baseboard is the main heat, a heat pump can cool in summer and also relieve part of the winter load.
### Historic houses

Stow lists several buildings on the National Register of Historic Places, among them the Walcott-Whitney House, Tenney Homestead and Hapgood House. Houses of that character can be hard to duct, and a ductless system avoids cutting into old framing and plaster.
### Humidity and size
An oversized unit cools fast and then cycles off before it has dried the air. Sizing should follow the house, including insulation, windows and the rooms that face the afternoon sun.
### The utility

Hudson Light & Power Department supplies Stow's electricity. A large new system may need an electrical upgrade, and the utility is who to ask about service capacity. See the [heat pump page](/cities/stow/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) for rebate paths.

faq.q: Can I cool just the upstairs of my Stow house?
faq.a: Yes. A ductless head or two upstairs can cool bedrooms without cooling the whole house. If the house has ducts, a zoned system is another option. A visit shows which fits the layout, where the line set could run and whether the electrical panel can take the added load.

faq.q: Is it worth adding central air to a house from the largest age band?
faq.a: Sometimes. It turns on whether duct routes exist. Stow has 707 homes in its largest age band, built from 1960 through 1979, so the question comes up often. Where new duct runs would mean opening finished walls and ceilings, ductless can be the neater answer.

faq.q: What causes an air conditioner to run without cooling?
faq.a: Typical culprits are a coil clogged with dirt, a capacitor that gave out, a slow refrigerant leak or a blocked filter. A dead compressor in an aging unit is a different and larger problem. Ask for the estimate in writing so the small repairs and the large ones are kept apart.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Hudson Light & Power Department, a municipal utility, supplies Stow's electricity, so Mass Save generally reaches only gas-heated homes. The 1,404 oil and 219 propane homes should ask the utility about its own program.
body: ## Two paths in a municipal electric town

Where a municipal company supplies the power, Mass Save heat pump rebates are generally limited to homes that heat with natural gas from a Mass Save sponsor. Everyone else looks to Hudson Light & Power's own program. Mass Save's detailed terms are on the [general heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Gas homes
Stow's 661 gas homes, 25.3%, are the group Mass Save is likeliest to reach. A heat pump there is often a cooling and mild-weather heating choice, with the gas unit kept for cold weather.
### Oil and propane homes

The 1,404 oil homes and 219 propane homes would generally look to Hudson Light & Power. Oil ranks 15th and propane 12th among the 50 towns, so this is a large group. We have no figures for the utility's program, so call it before planning around any amount.
### Electric homes
The 311 homes on electric heat, 11.9%, are where a heat pump replaces resistance heat. The utility is the same one that supplies their power, which makes it the natural first call.
### Age and weatherization

A home built in 2000 or later passes one test of Mass Save's weatherization rules. In Stow that covers 577 homes, 22.1%, while 1,503, 57.5%, predate 1980. Homes in that older group would likely start with an assessment and some air sealing.
### Questions for the utility

Ask Hudson Light & Power whether its program covers your current fuel, what equipment it accepts, how large the incentive can be and when applications close. Get the answers in writing before ordering equipment, since municipal programs set their own terms.
### Small fuel groups
Another 12 Stow homes list other fuels or coal and 6 list wood. For those households a heat pump is a bigger change, and it is worth deciding what the stove or other appliance will do afterward.
### Shared buildings
With 432 units in multi-unit buildings, some heat pump decisions involve an owner or association. Mini-splits avoid new ducts, but outdoor equipment needs approval.
### Detached houses
Detached houses are 79.8% of Stow's stock. The [cooling page](/cities/stow/air-conditioning-installation-repair) shows how ductless fits them.

faq.q: Who do I call first about a heat pump rebate in Stow?
faq.a: If you heat with oil, propane or electricity, start with Hudson Light & Power Department, which runs the municipal program. If you heat with natural gas, check masssave.com as well. Ask each for current terms and application deadlines, since programs change.

faq.q: Can a heat pump replace my oil boiler entirely?
faq.a: In a tight, well-insulated house it can. In many houses a heat pump carries most of the year and the boiler handles the coldest days. The home's heating load decides how much a heat pump can take, and that assessment comes before any system is quoted.

faq.q: Does Stow's age mix affect heat pump choice?
faq.a: It can. About 22.1% of Stow homes date from 2000 or later and are likelier to be tight, while the 1,503 older homes vary in insulation and air leakage. The older group may need sealing or insulation work before a whole-home system makes sense.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: With 1,404 Stow homes on oil and 219 on tank gas, yearly service means burner cleaning for most and a gas check for the rest. Every unit in town is occupied, so a failure is felt at once.
body: ## Service by fuel

An oil boiler or furnace is cleaned every year, from burner and nozzle to filter and heat exchanger, and then tested for combustion. Gas appliances, on a main or a tank, are checked at the burner, vent and connections. Electric and heat pump homes need attention at filters, coils and drains. Stow has all of these groups, with wood at just 6 homes.
### What an oil visit covers

- Clean the burner and heat exchanger
- Replace the nozzle and filter
- Test combustion, inspect the flue and tank lines
### What a gas or propane visit covers

- Check burner and flame
- Inspect venting
- Check gas connections and controls
### Equipment and housing age

The median Stow house was built in 1975, and 533 homes come from 1980 through 1999. Equipment from that era may already have been replaced once, and the schedule follows the age of the unit rather than the house.
### Owners, renters and timing

Owners hold 2,208 households and renters 405. Landlords who book the boiler ahead of the first cold week lower the odds of a no-heat call. Late summer suits heating work, and spring suits cooling checks.
### Larger buildings

Stow has 272 units in buildings of five or more and 141 in buildings of three or four. A building with one shared boiler puts many households behind a single machine, so the yearly visit protects all of them at once, and the owner or manager can schedule it ahead of the season.
### Older chimneys
The 472 Stow homes built in 1939 or earlier are likelier to have older masonry chimneys. A flue liner that no longer suits a new boiler is a common reason a replacement stalls.
### Heat pumps and cooling
Mini-splits and central air need clean filters, coils and drains, and an outdoor unit clear of leaves and snow. The 311 electric-heat homes are likelier to rely on this equipment all year.
### When to call early

Do not wait for the next annual visit if you notice an odd noise, a smell of oil or smoke, or a unit that keeps starting and stopping. Air handling outside the burner is covered on the [air quality page](/cities/stow/indoor-air-quality).

faq.q: How often should my Stow oil boiler be serviced?
faq.a: Every year, ahead of the heating season. Soot gradually coats the heat exchanger, which can lower efficiency or end in a cold-weather breakdown. Booking in late summer leaves time for a part to arrive if one is worn.

faq.q: Does a propane furnace need a yearly check?
faq.a: Yes, it is a good habit. A technician examines the burner, venting, controls and gas connections. With 219 homes on tank gas and a 12th-place rank among the 50 towns, propane equipment is a regular part of the service calendar here.

faq.q: What does a heat pump need each year?
faq.a: Clean filters, a look at the coils and condensate drains, and space around the outdoor unit. The work is lighter than burner service, though skipping it lets small problems grow. For a house that relies on a heat pump all year, a spring and a fall check are both sensible.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Stow's 2,613 homes range from 472 built in 1939 or earlier to 308 built since 2010, so air problems differ: older houses leak, newer ones are tighter. The Assabet River and Lake Boon make damp worth watching.
body: ## Air across every era of building

By the ACS 2022 counts, Stow has 472 homes (18.1%) from 1939 or earlier, 324 (12.4%) from 1940 to 1959, 707 (27.1%) from 1960 to 1979, 533 (20.4%) from 1980 to 1999 and 577 (22.1%) from 2000 on. Additions can add yet another era to a single house.
### Older houses

An older house exchanges air with the outdoors through gaps at windows, sills and attic floors, which thins out some pollutants and admits dust and damp. Renovation dust in a very old house is worth containing, and testing for lead paint or asbestos is a specialist's job.
### Newer houses

Houses from 2010 on, 308 in Stow, are likelier to have a tight shell. Humidity and cooking fumes stay inside such a house unless fresh air is supplied, so exhaust fans that discharge outdoors earn their keep.
### Water in the landscape

The Assabet River, Lake Boon, White's Pond and Elizabeth Brook are all part of Stow, and the river's flood of March 2010 reached 2,500 cubic feet per second. A basement that takes in water can use a dehumidifier for the air, but the water itself needs a separate fix.
### Other fuels

Wood heats 6 Stow homes and another 12 burn other fuels or coal. Solid-fuel appliances produce smoke and fine particles when the draft is poor, so a sound chimney and a stove that burns dry wood protect the air indoors.
### Dry winter air
Winter heating can dry indoor air. A humidifier on the system can ease that, and the humidity level is easy to check with a small hygrometer.
### Combustion safety
Venting matters for every fuel-burning appliance, and a carbon monoxide alarm on each level costs little. When an alarm goes off, get everyone outside and phone for help.
### Filters and ducts

Pick a filter the blower can handle, since a dense one starves airflow. Duct cleaning belongs to cases of visible dirt, mold or a renovation. The [tune-up page](/cities/stow/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups) covers the equipment side.

faq.q: Is the air in an older Stow house worse than in a newer one?
faq.a: Not by default. A leaky older house gets fresh air along with dust and damp, and a tight newer one holds humidity and fumes. Each can be improved once the cause is identified, and the fixes are different.

faq.q: Do I need my ducts cleaned?
faq.a: Only when there is a reason, such as mold, thick visible dirt or dust stirred up by a remodel. Examine the full system, including filter and return grilles, before deciding that cleaning is what would help.

faq.q: How do I control humidity in a damp basement?
faq.a: A dehumidifier sized to the space keeps the air drier, and gutters, grading and any leaks should be dealt with at the source. Keep the unit's drain clear and empty the bucket on schedule. A hygrometer shows whether the level stays in range.
